articles.title: Rochdale Local Plan Advances with Focus on Housing and Transport
articles.excerpt: The Rochdale Local Plan aims to shape the borough's development until 2039, focusing on nearly 11,000 new homes and improvements to transport hubs.
articles.content_html:
A new strategy to shape Rochdale's future has moved closer to implementation as the borough's Local Plan is set to undergo public consultation. The plan outlines how Rochdale will develop until 2039, with a focus on building nearly 11,000 new homes and transforming local transport hubs.

The Local Plan, which has been refined into a 175-page document, was approved by council leaders and is expected to be formally adopted in 2027. Initially, the plan required 20 per cent of new housing developments to be affordable, but this threshold has been adjusted to 15 per cent due to financial viability concerns. Councillor Daniel Meredith stated that this change does not reflect a reduced commitment to affordable housing, highlighting that the council has delivered 883 affordable homes in the past five years, exceeding previous targets.

Housing is a significant component of the Local Plan, with designated land for new developments already identified through the Places for Everyone strategy, which aims to create around 175,000 homes across Greater Manchester over the next two decades. The plan is expected to stimulate investment and redevelopment in Rochdale, particularly through the Atom Valley scheme, which aims to create 7,000 new homes and 20,000 jobs.

The Rochdale Rail Corridor Strategy is central to the Local Plan, proposing the reconfiguration of land around transport hubs along the Manchester to Leeds railway line. This initiative aims to create vibrant spaces for living, working, and recreation, focusing on stations in Rochdale, Castleton, Mills Hill, Smithy Bridge, Littleborough, and a new Slattocks station. The plan also includes improvements to walking and cycling routes, park and ride facilities, and community spaces, all intended to enhance the local economy.

articles.title: Backlash from British Pakistanis over Rochdale grooming gang ringleader's deportation
articles.excerpt: Ministers face criticism from British Pakistanis regarding plans to sanction Pakistan if it does not accept the return of Shabir Ahmed, the ringleader of the Rochdale grooming gang.
articles.content_html:
Ministers are facing backlash from British Pakistanis over threats to sanction Pakistan if it refuses to take back Shabir Ahmed, the ringleader of the Rochdale grooming gang. Ahmed, 73, was released from prison earlier this month after serving 14 years of a 22-year sentence for 30 child rape offences.

Senior figures within the Pakistani community in the UK are divided on whether Ahmed should be deported. Some have warned that any visa sanctions or aid cuts could damage relations between the two countries. Akhmed Yakoob, a solicitor from Birmingham, who previously stood against Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood in the last election, stated he would raise the issue if he stood again, accusing her of appeasing far-right sentiments by seeking Ahmed's deportation.

Yakoob described Ahmed as a dangerous criminal who has brought shame to the communities he lived in, arguing that Britain must take responsibility for its citizens. In response, a source close to Mahmood questioned whether Yakoob would prefer to have a grooming gang leader who sexually abused multiple children remain in the country.

The Government is pursuing Ahmed's deportation following his release, but Pakistan has yet to agree to accept him back. The situation is complicated by a 1971 immigration law loophole, which may hinder the deportation process.

articles.title: Hopwood Triangle Traffic Trial to Continue Pending Township Vote
articles.excerpt: Rochdale Council has confirmed that the Hopwood Triangle traffic calming trial will remain in place until a formal township vote is conducted to decide its future.
articles.content_html:
A traffic calming trial around the Hopwood Triangle in Heywood will continue pending a formal vote by the Heywood Township, Rochdale Council has announced. The trial, which introduced several changes to local roads, has faced significant criticism from motorists and residents since its implementation.

The measures include the closure of Middleton Road at its junction with Manchester Road near St John's Church, aimed at preventing drivers from using the route as a shortcut. Additionally, Magdala Street has been made one way towards Manchester Road, and new parking restrictions for heavy goods vehicles, along with a 20mph speed limit, have been introduced on surrounding residential roads.

North Heywood councillor Bev Place expressed disappointment that the trial would not end as soon as she had hoped. She stated that highways officers informed her that a township meeting must first vote to formally conclude the trial. Councillor Place is working to arrange an extraordinary meeting, as the next scheduled meeting is not until 22nd September.

In response to the ongoing concerns, a Rochdale Council spokesperson indicated that there is no set date for the removal of the traffic restrictions and that they are in discussions with contractors regarding the situation. Residents are encouraged to submit their views to the council's highways team via email to ensure their opinions are formally considered.

articles.title: 64 Rochdale food businesses rated 0 or 1 for hygiene
articles.excerpt: A total of 64 food businesses in Rochdale hold a food hygiene rating of 0 or 1, indicating urgent or major improvements are necessary, according to the Food Standards Agency.
articles.content_html:
A total of 64 food businesses in the Rochdale borough currently hold a food hygiene rating of 0 or 1, according to records from the Food Standards Agency checked on 29 July 2026. Five businesses are rated 0, where urgent improvement is necessary, while 59 are rated 1, indicating major improvement is necessary.

Among the businesses rated 0 are Yo 1 Stop, a retailer located at 1 Middleton Road, Heywood, which received its rating following an inspection on 22 June 2026. Other businesses rated 0 include Apple & Pears, a pub at Andover Avenue, and Wildbloods of Norden Limited, a retailer on Edenfield Road, both rated 0 after inspections in March 2026. Knockout Diner, a takeaway on Baillie Street, and Frozen Delights and Convenience, a restaurant on the same street, were also rated 0 after inspections in February and December 2025, respectively.

The businesses rated 1 include Davids, a takeaway on Dale Street, and Grillo, a takeaway on Heady Hill Road, both rated 1 after inspections on 30 June 2026. Other establishments with a rating of 1 include Denehurst Stores, Meanwood Stores, and several retailers on Oldham Road, all of which received their ratings in June 2026. Notable mentions also include Zam Zam Kitchen, a takeaway on Milkstone Road, and Marland Court, a caring premises, both rated 1 after inspections in June and May 2026, respectively.

The Food Standards Agency provides these ratings to inform the public about food hygiene standards. Businesses rated 0 or 1 are encouraged to make improvements to ensure compliance with hygiene regulations. The ratings serve as a guide for consumers when choosing where to eat or purchase food.

articles.title: Severely Neglected Toddler Rushed to Hospital After Social Services Case Closed
articles.excerpt: A 19-month-old girl was admitted to hospital in critical condition 19 days after social services closed her case, revealing severe neglect and malnutrition.
articles.content_html:
A 19-month-old girl, referred to as Child K1, was rushed to hospital in critical condition 19 days after social services closed her case, according to a recent Child Safeguarding Practice Review (CSPR) in Rochdale. The review reported that the toddler was found to be severely emaciated, weighing just 9.7lb (4.4kg), less than half the expected weight for her age, and covered in sores.

The review detailed that the child was severely dehydrated and had no fatty tissue on her body when she was admitted to critical care in February 2025. Medical professionals noted that she displayed "paper-thin skin" and had open pressure sores extending along her back, hips, and bottom. The case was closed despite warnings about a mother's neglect, who was only 17 when the child was born.

The review, conducted by expert reviewer Nicki Walker-Hall, highlighted that the toddler's mother had struggled with mental health issues and had avoided contact with social workers and health visitors. Following an anonymous tip in December 2024, social workers visited the home and confirmed the child's poor condition but were unable to secure consent for further intervention from the mother, leading to the case being closed due to insufficient evidence of significant harm.

Nineteen days after the case closure, the child was admitted to hospital, where medical staff noted a range of complications that could have led to death if not treated promptly. The findings of the review have prompted Rochdale Borough's Safeguarding Children Partnership to accept the conclusions and take action to address the issues identified.

articles.title: Rochdale Council Faces £15m Budget Deficit by 2029
articles.excerpt: Rochdale Council could face a £15m budget deficit by 2029 if no action is taken, according to the latest financial forecast presented at a town hall meeting.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Council is projected to face a budget deficit of £15.227 million by the financial year 2029/30 if no measures are implemented. The latest budget forecast, presented at a town hall meeting, highlights that this shortfall is anticipated due to wage increases, inflation, and rising costs in adult social care and children’s services.

The finance team has expressed uncertainty regarding the annual government funding settlement, which complicates future budgeting. Budget documents indicate a risk that the finance settlement for 2029/30 may not include a continuation of the Recovery Grant, which is currently confirmed only until 2028/29 and amounts to approximately £15 million.

In adult social care, the 'real living wage' is expected to rise beyond anticipated levels, further straining budgets. An additional allocation of £1.5 million per year has been factored into future costs. Overspending in children’s services has also exceeded initial forecasts, a trend noted in recent years, according to finance boss Sam Smith.

During the meeting on July 28, Councillor Daniel Meredith stated that efforts are underway to create new care homes and children’s homes, expressing optimism about addressing the challenges in these services. The council has made savings of £204.5 million from its revenue budget since 2010/11, but the projected gaps indicate that savings of £6 million will be necessary by 2028/29, increasing to £15 million by 2029/30.

articles.title: Phil Eckersley Promises Support for Greater Manchester Boroughs Ahead of Mayoral Election
articles.excerpt: Conservative mayoral candidate Phil Eckersley has pledged to enhance support for Greater Manchester's boroughs, addressing crime and housing issues in an interview.
articles.content_html:
Phil Eckersley, the Conservative candidate for Mayor of Greater Manchester, has pledged to provide more support to the boroughs of the region in an interview with the source. He expressed concern that too much focus has been placed on the city centre, leaving towns on the outskirts, including Rochdale, feeling neglected.

Eckersley highlighted the rise in crime in the boroughs, stating that residents are 'too scared to walk home after 8pm' due to fears of anti-social behaviour. He attributed part of this issue to the Greater Manchester Police, claiming they have not effectively addressed these concerns. He called for increased stop and searches and a greater police presence across the region, rather than just in the city centre.

In addition to crime, Eckersley aims to build more affordable homes throughout Greater Manchester, focusing on developing brownfield sites to protect green spaces. He also promised to support local businesses, asserting that he would be the 'most pro-business mayor Greater Manchester has ever had.'

Eckersley's policies align closely with those of Labour candidate Bev Craig, particularly regarding affordable housing and support for boroughs outside the city centre. However, he believes Labour has failed to deliver for the region during their time in control of the mayoralty since 2015. The Greater Manchester Mayoral by-election is scheduled for Thursday, 30th July.

articles.title: Three men sentenced for running Rochdale's 'Adam Line' drug operation
articles.excerpt: Three men have been sentenced for their roles in a Rochdale drug line that generated over £1 million a year, despite previous police efforts to dismantle it.
articles.content_html:
Three men have been sentenced for their involvement in a drug line in Rochdale known as the 'Adam Line', which reportedly generated over £1 million a year. The operation continued despite multiple police interventions aimed at shutting it down.

Haider Ali, 34, known as 'The Ghost', was identified as the controller of the drug line. He was arrested after police observed a suspected drug deal on Baron Street. Officers found £1,000 in cash and wraps of cocaine and heroin on him, along with 75 wraps of cocaine and 32 wraps of heroin in the vehicle he was in.

Alan Ronald Ohara, 47, referred to as 'Rocket Ronny', was the driver, while 17-year-old Shane Walsh acted as Ali's lieutenant, responsible for preparing drugs for sale. Evidence presented in court indicated that Walsh had been involved in drug dealing since he was 16, and had continued his activities even after being released on bail.

The court heard that messages on Ohara's phone suggested he was involved in the management of the operation and was considering starting his own drug line. The prosecution highlighted the exploitation of Walsh, who had faced personal challenges and was groomed into the drug culture. Prosecutor Craig MacGregor noted that the gang had previously engaged in serious criminal activities, including bribing witnesses and using violence.

John Morris, now 88, was just 18 years old when he participated in the tests conducted by the Ministry of Defence (MoD) at Christmas Island in the Pacific Ocean.

Morris is part of a group of veterans who have lodged a criminal complaint against the MoD, claiming they have been denied justice regarding the health issues they suffered as a result of the tests. Many veterans have reported serious medical problems and have called for an independent inquiry into their treatment. Burnham has previously supported the veterans' cause, stating that there is clear evidence of misconduct in public office.

Morris believes that Burnham's backing for a judicial review could lead to significant progress in their fight for recognition and compensation. He stated that the new Prime Minister has given him hope of achieving justice after years of campaigning. Morris and other veterans have expressed their frustration with the MoD's response, which has indicated that compensation is available through the War Pensions Scheme, but many feel this is insufficient.

The ongoing struggle for justice among those affected by the nuclear tests highlights the need for a thorough investigation into the treatment of veterans. Morris's comments reflect the sentiments of many who feel that their sacrifices have not been adequately acknowledged.
